rubric_notes: All must_include content present with verified sunids for a.22.1 and its five families; probable common ancestry correctly tied to superfamily level; explicit refusal to transfer nucleosome/DNA-wrapping function across families; family-level template advice. Linker histone (a.4.5.13 lineage) and H-NS (a.155.1) placements supported by bundle. Deduction: states HU/IHF and H-NS are 'unrelated to the histone fold' and named 'not for shared ancestry' as fact, an absence-of-homology assertion SCOPe does not make. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Full lineages with sunids match bundle. Correct superfamily-vs-fold distinction and family split interpretation. Explicitly refuses to transfer PR-ATP/histidine or MazG/(p)ppGpp roles; general Mg2+/acidic-motif chemistry presented as hypothesis only. Notes boundary difference and template unreliability; lists external evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Correct families with sunids, superfamily, fold, class, duplication comment and full c.55 superfamily list, all supported by evidence. Infers remote homology with a common ancestral ATPase core, homologous cleft ATP site and domain closure; refuses to transfer function, substrate, polymerization, chaperone activity, regulation, oligomeric state, cellular role; clearly separates family/superfamily/fold/class meanings and treats the shared RNase H-like motif alone as insufficient for homology. Transparent about which claims come from SCOPe records versus general knowledge. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

All three families correctly placed in a.25.1 with sunids matching bundle; superfamily comment quoted correctly; distinguishes superfamily homology from fold-only a.25 siblings; interprets as remote divergent homology; explicitly rejects transfer of function, metal identity and assembly; requires metal analysis, assays or family-level sequence match. No unsupported release claims. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Correct hierarchy, three family sunids, fold and superfamily comments, family annotations and Pfam mappings verified against bundle. Leads with correct conclusion (probable distant homologs, no shared copper/redox function), distinguishes superfamily homology from fold convergence, rejects transfer citing 'lacking the metal-binding site', separates background functional knowledge from SCOPe records, and lists conserved ligands plus structural, spectroscopic and redox evidence required. Complete.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. All family, superfamily and fold facts, including the full list of 15 d.15 superfamilies, match the bundle. Correct inference: same superfamily = probable common ancestry stronger than fold; fold alone is not evidence of homology. Rejects transferring conjugation, p97 binding and Ras/GTPase binding across families by name and lists family-level evidence needed (motifs, HMM hits, experimental data). Minor: does not explicitly say that separate superfamilies are not proof of non-homology, but not a material omission.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Correct families, sunids, fold comment, Pfam and KaiA annotations, sibling families, all supported. Superfamily-level homology distinguished from fold sharing and family-level closeness. Rejects phosphorylation transfer to KaiA-N and ODC wing, wing catalysis (PLP domain in c.67.1, outside c.23), decarboxylase/clock transfer to CheY, and GO/EC or active-site transfer via templates; explicitly states receiver activity is not implied for every c.23.1 member. Evidence needs and analysis limits stated.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. All stated classifications (b.84.5, b.84.5.1, protein sunids, siblings, PubMed citation, fold comment) supported by bundle. Clearly separates fold-level topology (possibly convergent) from superfamily-level ancestry, states homology within b.84.5/b.84.5.1 for V1 and A1 bulge domains, says common ancestry with other b.84 superfamilies is 'neither asserted nor ruled out', lists what evidence would change placement, and rejects function/template transfer. Background reading of the PMID flagged as such.

Fold, sunids, three superfamilies, and fold comment supported by bundle. Correctly separates fold from superfamily, offers convergence as a possibility while stating SCOPe simply lacked sufficient evidence to merge, rejects homology/function/template/representative transfer, and names sequence/profile similarity, shared unusual structural features, and ligand-position checks as needed evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct families, superfamily, fold, sunids, fold annotation, family comment and PF02254, all supported. Superfamily interpreted as probable remote homology from shared core and glycine-rich loop, not sequence; families as non-close relatives with divergent context. Explicit refusal to transfer oxidoreductase activity, zinc, ligand identity or gating; notes similar nucleotide binding in neighbouring folds does not prove ancestry; family-level templates; external evidence required. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct lineage and identifiers, correct conclusion that same family in class k does not imply homology, good transfer limits. However it never retrieved or cites the family 100905 'not a true family' annotation and explicitly states the caveat comes only from background knowledge about class k; the decisive explicit annotation (must_include 2 and 3) is missing. 'No common ancestor can exist' is slightly overstated.

Meets all must_include: 1.69 separate fold c.137.1.1 vs c.23.14.1; 2.08 d1t1ja1 (A:1-118) c.23.14.2 and d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1 sharing c.23.14 as lowest common node; explicit statement that a new-fold protein was recognised as a divergent superfamily member implying probable common ancestry, stronger than fold similarity. Distinguishes tag-domain split (d1t1ja2/d1t1jb2 l.1.1.1) from biological change. Evidence bundle (1.69 and 2.08 parents, annotations, homology) supports claims. Notes 1.73 already shows c.23.14.2 without wrongly claiming it as the first release. Limits stated. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Complete and well evidenced: artifact lineage, d1a14h1 lineage, both sequences (QVQLQQSG tag segment; AELVKPGAS... domain) all supported by bundle. Rejects tag similarity as homology evidence, explains l-class levels as labels. Adds a well-hedged caveat that QVQLQQSG matches VH FR1 and may be primer-encoded, without overriding the SCOPe classification, and states what would be needed to resolve it. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1; 2026-10-14.

Correct before/after: 1.75 and 2.03 whole-chain d1acca_ (43828, f.11.1.1); 2.04 onward and 2.08 two domains with correct sids, sunids, boundaries and sccs, in different classes. Uses the Kluyveromyces marxianus beta-glucosidase PA14 protein under b.179.1.1 as concrete evidence of module reuse, and bars reciprocal function transfer between toxin and glycosidase. Search advice covers per-domain assignment, release-specific subsets, coverage checks, and the caveat that the 225/226 boundary is a curated assignment. Asserts the curators' motive for the split without supporting evidence, a minor overreach that does not change the conclusion.

All must_include met with bundle-supported identifiers, boundaries, sccs and family names. Mosaic interpretation with group II intron origin flagged as literature, superfamily = probable ancestry, no function transfer, class membership correctly explained as not indicating separate origins, Jab1/MPN gap noted, sunid-based age inference honestly flagged. Opening sentence says each domain is in a different class but the answer later correctly lists four classes (a, c, d, e); internal inconsistency only. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14.

Complete: correct shared lineage with sunids, lengths 51/373/752, the 'single repeat' comment, the 're' inconsistency flag quoted verbatim, and the family repeat unit 4cj9 A:259-292 with coordinates valid only for d4cj9a_. Explains that repeat count is not domain count, that fold-level match alone would not prove homology, and that the non-repeat N/C-terminal regions fall outside this classification. Notes the asymmetry that the repeat representative carries no 're' flag and treats it as an annotation artifact rather than biology. Function and template caveats are explicit. Evaluator: Claude SCOPe benchmark grader, 2026-10-14.

Correct, supported metadata and periodic 2.08-2026-08-16. Cites stable 2.08 pinned in every call, rejects 'current'/'latest', records exact periodic identifier and retrieval date when results depend on post-freeze entries. Periodic semantics: dated update on 2.08 base adding newer PDB entries mostly by automated methods, not a new curated stable, stable label is the fixed citable snapshot. Clearly flags which parts come from general knowledge versus the endpoint. Complete.

Meets all must_include items with bundle support: same lineage for all three; fragment comment and 'ms' flag; four-helix fold definition versus three-helix fragments resembling a spectrin repeat; a.47 assignment of fragments inferred from complete homologous structures; d1dn1b_ automated match to d3c98b_ on obsolete 1dn1. Correctly frames the fragment/full-domain relationship as family-level homology, not fold similarity, rejects STAT and spectrin homology inferences, and limits representative choice, conformation and function transfer; notes release scope. The 'comparison tool' result is not in the bundle but its content (lowest shared level = family, 'ms' caveat) matches retrieved annotations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct framing: NAD(P) binding as shared function not ancestry; divergence supported only within superfamily/family; c.3/c.4 deeper ancestry noted as debated and unasserted; convergence described as the simplest explanation rather than proven. Multi-domain enzymes (b.35.1 class b, d.81.1 class d) used to show that 'dehydrogenase' is not a lineage. Evidence integration complete (PSI-BLAST/HHpred, DALI/FATCAT whole-core with strand order, same cofactor position, idiosyncratic features, SCOPe assignment). All sunids and lineages supported by parents endpoints. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Both release states are correct and evidenced: 2.04 lowest shared node is class b with ColG in b.23.2 under CUB-like b.23 and Cry3A in b.18.1.3 under b.18.1, and from 2.05 through 2.08 ColG sits in new family b.18.1.36 (sunid 267607) with the domain sunid unchanged while Cry3A remains b.18.1.3, so the families stay distinct. Notes that fold, superfamily and family assignments all changed and that the other Cry3A domains in f.1.3.1 and b.77.2.1 are unaffected. Uses the retrieved family comment citing the relevant publication and identifies the linked Cry4Ba domain as belonging to the same family as Cry3A domain III. Explicitly says a shared sandwich fold alone would not prove ancestry, that the claim rests on curated structural plus functional evidence, that collagen binding, Ca dependence, receptor or glycan specificity and toxicity must not be transferred, and that single domains are representatives of a classification statement rather than of every homologue. Evaluator: Claude, 2026-10-14.

Complete and fully evidence-backed: lineage with sunids, comments, domain-level non-inherited hf with exact definition, homology_implied_by_level, and retrieved quality values (1p7j 2.1 A R 0.20 SPACI 0.442; 1ztr NMR effective 4 A, SPACI 0.0024, WHAT_CHECK Z-scores). Keeps homology by sequence, explains fold label as inherited not verified, rejects geometry/function transfer, treats quality as representativeness not homology, addresses leakage and hf stratification, lists external evidence needed. L16A recollection is hedged.

All must_include met: family homology retained (flag is data-quality caveat, not demotion to fold level); fr flag with 99 vs 50 residues and named missing segments; alignment scores biased in both normalisations; prefer complete unflagged d1uc6a1 or unflagged tissue-factor domain; fragments excluded/down-weighted in diversity stats while still counting for taxonomic diversity; no function transfer. Weaknesses: no quality values retrieved for either entry, and claims SPACI/AEROSPACI selection 'penalizes fragmentary chains' although those scores are entry-level and do not measure domain completeness. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Correct recommendation and semantics: family = homology claim (~30% or strong structure+function), superfamily = probable ancestry, fold = geometric statement; new fold only if core topology differs; classification is a revisable hypothesis at the strongest evidence-supported level; structural scores alone insufficient; no cross-fold function transfer. Convergence stated as a possibility. d.58 example (sunid 54861; d.58.1/6/7/9/10) supported by bundle.

Correct class/fold/superfamily/family identifiers with sunids and fold annotation supported. Distinguishes fold-level geometric similarity from superfamily homology, infers shared ancestral core and general mechanism, and refuses transfer of substrate class, recognition determinants, regulation, and inhibitor sensitivity. Evidence list covers family-level assignment with boundary checks, structure-aware alignment of catalytic/substrate residues, biochemistry, substrate-bound structures, regulatory elements, and orthology.
